sections.name: File setup, LIVE_SLUGS
sections.title: Live industry list and setup
sections.what: Loads the list of industries marked as live and builds a set of their short codes for quick checks. Only these industries can be selected or benchmarked on the Reality Scan page.
sections.why: Likely reason: the page should offer only industries that are ready to show, so the status flag controls what users see.
sections.watch_out: An industry is included only when its status is exactly live. Renaming or changing that status in the shared list removes it from this page.

sections.name: parseSelectionFromSearch
sections.title: Reading the industry selection from the URL
sections.what: Reads the industries parameter from the web address, drops any code that is not a live industry, removes repeats, and returns the clean list. An empty or fully invalid address returns no selection.
sections.why: The code says the web address is the source of truth, so back, forward, refresh and shared links keep the same view.
sections.watch_out: Unknown or non-live codes are dropped silently. A link with only invalid codes falls back to the picker with no warning.

sections.name: DatumHeader
sections.title: Top header with login status
sections.what: Draws the header with the CPD logo link and the Reality Scan label. When an industry view is open it adds a back button. It shows the signed-in user's name and role with a log out button, or a log in link when no one is signed in.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The header shows the user's identifier and role on screen, so anyone looking at the screen can see who is signed in.

sections.name: DatumResults
sections.title: Results view with one tab per industry
sections.what: When industries are selected, shows a tab for each one. Each tab displays the Analysis component for that industry. The first selected industry opens by default. The tabs reset whenever the selection changes.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the user compare industries side by side without leaving the page.
sections.watch_out: The tab list is rebuilt from the URL selection, so changing the selected industries resets which tab is open.

sections.name: Datum (part 1)
sections.title: Selection state and project counts
sections.what: Keeps the picker's working selection and asks the server for a project count for each live industry. It adds the counts into a total and tracks whether counts are still loading. Toggling an industry adds or removes it from the working selection. Running the scan moves the selection into the web address.
sections.why: The code says the picker selection stays in memory until Run is pressed, so half-finished choices are not lost while the user browses.
sections.watch_out: Missing counts are treated as zero in the total, so the total can look too low while counts are still loading.

sections.name: Datum: if
sections.title: Industry picker grid by sector
sections.what: Shows the Reality Scan title, a guide button and a demo link. Below that, it lists every industry grouped by sector, each as a tile with its count, showing whether it is selected. Clicking a tile toggles it.
sections.why: Likely reason: grouping by sector helps users find an industry quickly among many.
sections.watch_out: All industries are shown, but only live ones can be toggled. A tile for a non-live industry looks like a normal tile and does nothing when clicked.

sections.name: Datum (part 3)
sections.title: Bottom bar and run button
sections.what: Shows a sticky bar at the bottom with a summary of how many industries are selected and a Run Reality Scan button. The button is disabled until at least one industry is selected. It shows the combined project total once counts have loaded.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The button can show zero projects while counts are still loading, because the shown total only reads the counts that have arrived so far.

summary: Results page that shows one tab per chosen industry, using the industries listed in the web address, with a header that shows the sign-in state.
purpose: Lets a visitor compare one or more live industries side by side in tabs, each tab showing that industry's analysis.
why: Reason not stated in the code for the overall design. The visible parts show the tabs are built from the selection in the web address, so the page can be shared by link.
how: 1. Reads the industries parameter from the web address and keeps only codes that are live and not repeated. 2. Draws a header with a link back to the home page, a sign-in or sign-out control, and a Industries button when a way back is given. 3. Creates one tab per chosen industry and puts the Analysis component inside each tab. The later part of the file was not visible, so any further steps are unknown.
inputs: The industries parameter in the web address, a comma-separated list of industry codes. The signed-in user from the authentication hook.
outputs: A results page with a tab for each valid industry. Nothing visible is saved or sent to the server.
risks: Codes that are not live are dropped without any message, so a typo gives a shorter page with no explanation. Only the first 120 of 272 lines were visible, so other risks cannot be judged.
debug: If the page is empty, check the industries parameter in the address and confirm each code is marked LIVE in the shared industry list. If the header shows the wrong user, check the useAuth hook. The bottom of the file was not provided, so read the final render directly.
